page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server built on the x86_64 architecture. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, delivering 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 3840 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong computational performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests placing in the top 25%. PassMark CPU scores, including extended instructions and physics tests, also rank in the top 25%. While cached small-block memory bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths are in the top 10%, reaching 458.63 GB/sec and 223.24 GB/sec respectively. Other operations, such as Redis SET, static web serving throughput, and LLM inference for small and medium models, perform within average ranges.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:8 and the large local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound and storage-intensive workloads. It provides a balanced qualitative cost-to-resource profile by combining dedicated AMD EPYC cores with substantial high-speed storage. This configuration is well-suited for database hosting, memory-intensive data processing, large-scale web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
